# Link Alloy 0.0.3 — experimental alpha

**The combined-throughput issue is not resolved.** This alpha is published for continued testing with the user's approval. It must not be presented as a verified download-speed boost.

## Download and run

Download **Link Alloy Portable.exe**, save it in a writable folder, and run as administrator. No ZIP or installer is required. The official Wintun runtime is embedded and extracted beside the executable when needed. License texts are available in Settings. Windows WebView2 is required. This application is unsigned.

## Changes

- Refreshed Windows UI with clearer typography, consistent icons, combined/per-link traffic, download-share indicators, and a Mbps/MiB/s preference.
- Application, network-link, connection-state, and service-domain filters in Connections.
- TLS service grouping separates supported content connections from account/control connections within the same application. Inspection is bounded, preserves the original destination and consumed bytes, and does not decrypt application data or install certificates.
- Allocation history is preserved when unrelated IP-family health changes occur; a cohort resets only when its own eligible links or weights change.
- Regression coverage for interleaved services, 2/3/4 adapters, persistent HTTP/2 transfers, verified end-to-end TLS, fallback, cancellation, and malformed input.
- Local bounded speed-check and read-only engine-log collection utilities. Diagnostic payload is discarded rather than written to disk.

## Known performance limitation

Short, sequential measurements on 4 November showed:

| Download test | Measured Mbps |
| --- | ---: |
| Ethernet directly | 94–124 |
| Wi-Fi directly | 30–31 |
| Timed HTTPS transfer through Link Alloy | approximately 87 |
| Steam before pausing | approximately 105–109 |

Steam's content sockets were evenly assigned across both physical links in the observed run, but useful traffic remained uneven. The controlled tunnel sample was below Ethernet alone. These samples do not isolate engine overhead from CDN/provider variability; they do establish that the current performance acceptance criterion has not passed. Steam logged failures obtaining fresh download sources. The post-resume comparison was interrupted and remains incomplete.

## Further testing

Pause the download, fully exit the launcher, stop the previous tunnel, and close the old app before launching this version. Start the tunnel, reopen the launcher, and resume. For Steam, filter Connections for `steamcontent.com` and compare sustained per-link payload progress. A short pause can reuse existing HTTP/2 sockets and retain their assignments.

Existing TCP connections are not split across links or transparently migrated. ICMP and fragmented packets remain unsupported. Physical link-loss, forced-crash recovery, signing, and successful sustained throughput validation remain open stable-release gates. Release retention keeps the two newest published releases while preserving source tags.
